facts.raw_span: 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining
Extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (hematoxylin-eosin stain)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses with eosinophils, is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses with eosinophils, are also consistent with Sweet syndrome.

The patient's presentation of extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration, along with a history of difficulty walking due to skin lesions, could be consistent with eczema herpeticum, although the negative HIV test and lack of other specific findings make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could be consistent with bullous pemphigoid, although the lack of specific findings such as blistering makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with a history of difficulty walking due to skin lesions, could be consistent with psoriasis, although the lack of specific findings such as silvery scales makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with a history of difficulty walking due to skin lesions, could be consistent with dermatitis herpetiformis, although the lack of specific findings such as blistering makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses with eosinophils, could be consistent with leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with a history of difficulty walking due to skin lesions, could be consistent with granuloma faciale, although the lack of specific findings such as granulomas makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with a history of difficulty walking due to skin lesions, could be consistent with erythema elevatum diutinum, although the lack of specific findings such as neutrophilic infiltrates makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses with eosinophils, could be consistent with neutrophilic dermatosis.
It explains the dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration found in the histopathology results.
